def workshop_schedules(jobs):
    """
    A workshop has two machines: a cutter C and a polisher P.  There are n
    candidate jobs, jobs[i] = (a, b): job i needs the cutter for a minutes
    and afterwards the polisher for b minutes.

    Constraints: 1 <= n <= 24 and 1 <= a, b <= 12 for every job (all ints).

    If some set of jobs is accepted, they are processed in a single chosen
    sequence: the cutter works on the accepted jobs one at a time in that
    sequence with no idle time required between them, and each job may start
    on the polisher only after BOTH (1) its own cutting is finished and
    (2) the polisher has finished every earlier job of the sequence.  Each
    machine handles one job at a time; jobs are not interruptible.  The
    makespan of the accepted set is the minute at which the polisher finishes
    the last job, starting from minute 0, minimized over all possible
    sequences of the accepted jobs.

    Return a list res of n integers where res[k-1] is the minimum possible
    makespan over all ways to accept EXACTLY k of the n jobs (and sequence
    them optimally).  There are no ties to break: the answer is a unique
    number.  jobs must not be modified.

    >>> workshop_schedules([(5, 7)])
    [12]
    >>> workshop_schedules([(3, 2), (1, 4)])
    [5, 7]
    >>> workshop_schedules([(2, 3), (3, 3), (4, 1)])
    [5, 7, 10]
    """
